overview: A Department of State list of papers, prepared or filed on October 12, 1945, inventories earlier correspondence concerning petroleum exploration in Taiwan (then Formosa). The listed papers concern a proposed geophysical-exploration program for the Nippon Mining Company of Tokyo, a request by the National Geophysical Company for guidance on U.S. regulations and policy, and advice from the Department of Commerce that oil-well drilling machinery did not then require an export license, while declining to comment on the proposed undertaking itself.

people.name: John M. Temperton
people.role: Representative of the National Geophysical Company

subfiles.title: List of papers concerning petroleum in Formosa
subfiles.about: An administrative list identifies earlier correspondence about American participation in petroleum exploration in Formosa and the export of drilling machinery.
subfiles.summary: The sheet records an inquiry concerning a geophysical-exploration program sought by the Nippon Mining Company of Tokyo and a request for information about U.S. regulation and policy toward the undertaking. It also notes correspondence involving Commerce Department official Sinnott and the National Geophysical Company’s John M. Temperton. According to the précis, no export license was then required for oil-well drilling machinery, although the government offered no comment on the proposed project. The underlying papers appear to date from December 1940 and January 1941 but are not reproduced on this page.

interest: The page is useful as a compact archival roadmap to correspondence that is apparently absent from the surviving file segment. It documents the intersection of Japanese petroleum development in colonial Taiwan, prospective American technical assistance, and U.S. export controls immediately before the Pacific War. The reference to both a proposed geophysical survey and oil-well machinery may help historians reconstruct commercial contacts between American technical firms and Japanese mining interests during 1940–1941.
